title: Addison Disease: Clinical Clues and Hyperpigmentation
subject: Medical Triads
preview: Primary adrenal insufficiency may produce fatigue, weight loss, postural symptoms, hyponatremia and increased pigmentation.
quickRevision: Primary adrenal insufficiency may produce fatigue, weight loss, postural symptoms, hyponatremia and increased pigmentation.
Hyperkalemia and salt craving can reflect mineralocorticoid deficiency; acute adrenal crisis may feature shock.
Diagnosis uses appropriate cortisol and ACTH assessment, often with stimulation testing in a suitable setting.

sections.title: Recognize the pattern
points: Primary adrenal insufficiency may produce fatigue, weight loss, postural symptoms, hyponatremia and increased pigmentation.
Hyperpigmentation is related to elevated ACTH in primary rather than typical secondary adrenal failure.

sections.title: Exam trap — avoid this mistake
points: A hypotensive patient with suspected adrenal crisis needs urgent clinical management, not delayed care while awaiting tests.
